premise.en: Daniel Reyes, a documentary photographer who lived on ‘someday,’ and Hugo Lindqvist, a parks facilities manager who stopped waiting, broke up ten years ago with no villain but timing. Their friend Joanie hands them the keys to a camper named Marjorie and a six-hour route home. No one sabotaged them; no one gets the decade back. You decide whether Daniel offers a real plan, a real apology, or a real goodbye.

en: A camper van named Marjorie has to be back in the city by six. Joanie, who owns Marjorie, has booked exactly two drivers. They haven’t spoken in ten years.
I’m already in the driver’s seat with the mirrors set. I got here at seven-forty. Some things don’t change.
I load my gear: two camera bags, a tripod, a cooler, a duffel. The back fills up fast.
You still drive like you’re late.
You still pack like you’re moving in.
Joanie’s note on the dash: ‘Two routes. Highway 9, four hours. Or the old county road, past the lake. You two know which lake.’
The lake where I said ‘someday’ so many times it stopped being a word.
Your call. I’m just the one who’s actually on time.
zh: 一辆名叫Marjorie的露营车，六点前必须回到城里。车主Joanie只订了两名司机。这两个人已经十年没说过话。
我已经坐在驾驶座上，后视镜都调好了。我七点四十就到了。有些事是不会变的。
我往车上搬东西：两个相机包、一个三脚架、一个冷藏箱、一个行李袋。后舱很快就满了。
你收拾行李还像要搬进来住。
仪表台上是Joanie的字条：“两条路。9号公路，四小时。或者走老县道，经过那片湖。你们俩知道是哪片湖。”
就是那片湖。我在那儿说了太多次“总有一天”，说到它都不像个词了。

en: Rest stop. Vending machines, a picnic table, one discouraged maple. Daniel comes back from the van with something in his hand.
I set it on the table like evidence: sour cherry licorice, the long ropes. He used to go through a bag a day.
I look at it a long time. I haven’t eaten sugar like that since my dentist gave me a speech.
My knees are forty. The rest is trying.
I had a version of you in my bag.
You can make room for this one.
